title: Mixed-Type Tabular Data Synthesis with Score-based Diffusion in Latent Space
summary: Argues that diffusion applied directly to mixed-type tables must contend with one-hot categorical columns that do not diffuse well, and proposes TabSyn, which first learns a joint continuous latent space with a transformer variational autoencoder and then runs score-based diffusion inside it, so that a single Gaussian process covers numerical and categorical columns at once and sampling needs few steps. CTGAN and TVAE are the GAN and VAE baselines among the seven methods it is measured against across six datasets.
affiliations: Amazon Web Services; George Mason University
evidence: the baselines paragraph states the first two of seven comparisons are the classical GAN and VAE models, CTGAN and TVAE, both from Xu et al. 2019; the related-work section credits Xu et al. with proposing CTGAN and TVAE to deal with imbalanced categorical features; the results tables report CTGAN and TVAE column-wise distribution scores on Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic, Beijing and News

title: TabMT: Generating tabular data with masked transformers
summary: Applies masked transformers to tabular generation, treating each cell as a token to be predicted from the unmasked remainder, with ordered embeddings for numerical fields and a dedicated category for missing values so that incomplete tables train without imputation. TVAE is one of the four generators it is measured against, selected as the strongest VAE-based tabular baseline, and the comparison covers downstream classification accuracy across a range of datasets alongside correlation-error and privacy analyses.
evidence: the prior-methods paragraph states that four techniques are selected, one from each major family, and describes TVAE as coming from one of the first deep tabular generation papers which introduced both a GAN and a VAE, with the VAE chosen as the strongest VAE tabular generator; the results table reports TVAE alongside CTabGAN+, REaLTabFormer and TabDDPM on downstream accuracy across datasets

title: MissDiff: Training Diffusion Models on Tabular Data with Missing Values
summary: Trains diffusion models directly on tables that contain missing values, masking the regression loss for unobserved entries so the score is learned without first imputing, and shows the resulting estimator is consistent under missing-at-random assumptions where impute-then-generate pipelines are not. CTGAN and TVAE appear once, inside the paper's description of a diffusion baseline reported to outperform them by a large margin; neither is run here.
evidence: the baselines section describes STaSy as the state-of-the-art diffusion model on tabular data which outperforms MedGAN, VEEGAN, CTGAN, TVAE, TableGAN, OCTGAN and RNODE by a large margin, which is the only mention of either model in the body; the CTGAN paper appears in the bibliography and no experiment in the paper trains or samples it

title: How Realistic Is Your Synthetic Data? Constraining Deep Generative Models for Tabular Data
summary: Points out that deep tabular generators routinely emit rows violating background knowledge that always holds in the real data, and proposes a differentiable constraint layer that is appended to any generator so that generated samples are projected onto the feasible region during training and sampling, evaluated over six tasks with hand-specified constraint sets. CTGAN and TVAE are two of the five generators the layer is applied to, each becoming a named constrained variant, C-CTGAN and C-TVAE, whose constraint-violation rate and downstream utility are reported against the unmodified originals.
affiliations: Vienna University of Technology; University of Oxford
evidence: the experimental settings state that five deep generative models were used, WGAN, TableGAN, CTGAN, TVAE and GOGGLE, and that each model was augmented by the constraint layer, resulting in C-WGAN, C-TableGAN, C-CTGAN, C-TVAE and C-GOGGLE; the results tables report constraint violation rates and utility for CTGAN against C-CTGAN and TVAE against C-TVAE across the six datasets. Note the constraint layer is model-agnostic, so C-CTGAN is one of five parallel variants rather than a CTGAN-specific construction
needs: confirm derivative_work at importance 4 for a model-agnostic layer that yields a named CTGAN variant among several, rather than the usual 5

title: Deep Generative Models, Synthetic Tabular Data, and Differential Privacy: An Overview and Synthesis
summary: Synthesises the literature on deep generative models for tabular data under differential privacy, setting variational autoencoders, normalizing flows, GANs and diffusion models in a common probabilistic notation and then tracing how each has been fitted with privacy guarantees, with attention to where the tabular setting breaks assumptions carried over from images. CTGAN is presented as the reference set of refinements for the tabular GAN, named for mode-specific normalization and conditioning vectors and for carrying both across to the VAE in the same work; later methods are described by what they replace in it, such as an inverse-CDF transform standing in for its mode-specific normalization. Nothing is run.
evidence: the section on GANs for tabular data states that several refinements of a basic GAN approach are considered in the conditional tabular GAN approach of Xu et al. 2019, namely mode-specific normalization and conditioning vectors, and that the same work applies these to VAE models; a following paragraph describes Li et al.'s inverse-CDF GAN as replacing the mode-specific normalization in CTGAN with a transformation based on an estimated cumulative distribution function
